extracted.intended_audience: prospective GCF applicants, accredited entities, climate finance stakeholders and policy audiences
extracted.subtask_description: High-level criteria and classification dimensions used by the Green Climate Fund to guide investments and to organise/browse approved projects (policy aims, allocation targets, thematic/result-area categories, access modalities, priority groups, regions, sizes, statuses, and approval periods).

rubrics_metrics.name: GCF investment objective — maximum impact in developing world
rubrics_metrics.description: GCF’s investments are aimed at achieving maximum impact in the developing world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement of strategic purpose: investments should deliver impactful climate action where it's needed most; projects in developing countries are prioritized. (Referenced on the projects list as the Fund's overarching aim.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Support paradigm shifts in mitigation and adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting paradigm shifts in both mitigation and adaptation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should contribute at a scale or in a manner that enables systemic change (a 'paradigm shift') in mitigation and/or adaptation pathways rather than only incremental change.

rubrics_metrics.name: 50:50 mitigation vs. adaptation balance target
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund aims for a 50:50 balance between mitigation and adaptation investments over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation target to guide portfolio composition: over time the portfolio should average equal shares of mitigation and adaptation funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: 50% adaptation-floor for particularly vulnerable countries
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund aims for a floor of 50 percent of the adaptation allocation for particularly vulnerable countries, including Least Developed Countries (LDCs), Small Island Developing States (SIDS), and African States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy commitment to prioritize adaptation funding for especially vulnerable groups of countries; implies eligible projects from these groups should receive at least half of adaptation allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project theme classification (Adaptation / Cross-cutting / Mitigation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each project is classified by theme: Adaptation, Cross-cutting, or Mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to categorise and filter projects; projects should align clearly to one or more themes to reflect intended climate objective(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project type (Private sector / Public sector)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects are identified by type: Private sector or Public sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification used for portfolio reporting and filtering; indicates implementing modality and likely accreditation/finance instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Result area alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects are mapped to result areas such as Buildings, cities, industries, and appliances; Ecosystems and ecosystem services; Energy generation and access; Forests and land use; Health, food, and water security; Infrastructure and built environment; Livelihoods of people and communities; Transport.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should align with one or more result areas to demonstrate expected outcomes and to facilitate results-based management and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access modality (Direct National / Direct Regional / International)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filter and classification by access modality: Direct (National), Direct (Regional), International.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates whether the project is accessed via national entities, regional arrangements, or international accredited entities; relevant for eligibility, oversight, and implementation arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority group targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects can be associated with Priority Groups: African States, Least Developed Countries, Small Island Developing States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates special prioritization and reporting for projects benefiting these groups; relates to the Fund’s commitments to vulnerable countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic region
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects are associated with regions such as Africa; Asia and the Pacific; Eastern Europe, Central Asia, and the Middle East; Latin America and the Caribbean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geographic classification used for portfolio analysis, regional targeting, and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project size classification (Large / Medium / Small / Micro)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects are classified by size: Large, Medium, Small, Micro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Size category informs eligibility for certain modalities or instruments and is used in filtering and portfolio composition analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project status (Approved / Cancelled / Completed / Lapsed / Terminated / Under implementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects carry a status label such as Approved, Cancelled, Completed, Lapsed, Terminated, or Under implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status is used to indicate lifecycle stage of a project for monitoring, reporting, and stakeholder information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval/period tagging (Board period identifiers B.xx)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects are associated with Board/approval periods listed as B.44, B.43, B.42, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Period tags identify the board meeting or approval cycle when a project was considered/approved and support temporal filtering and record-keeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal filtering (by year/date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects can be filtered by date/year (e.g., 2015–2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables searching and reporting by year of approval or activity; useful for trend analysis and portfolio timelines.
